name: Landscape of the Pico Island Vineyard Culture
description: On Pico, in Portugal's Azores, vines grow in thousands of tiny rectangular plots called currais, each enclosed by black volcanic stone walls. The walls run in long parallel lines inland from the rocky shore, shielding the grapes from Atlantic wind and salt spray. Winegrowing here goes back to the 15th century, and you can still see the old wine cellars, manor houses, churches and small harbours.
